3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant/writ petitioner and the learned counsels appearing for the respondents and perused the materials available on record.

4. The said writ petition was heard along with three other connected matters and by common order dated 09.10.2017, the same was disposed of, granting liberty to the writ petitioners to file necessary appeal under Section 3- G(5) of the Act before the concerned authority, namely, District Collector within a period of two weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of that order and on such appeal being filed, the same shall be entertained without raising any objections as to the limitation aspect and suitable orders be passed thereon on merits and in accordance with law as expeditiously as possible, after affording due opportunity of hearing to the petitioner and the respondents.
Without exhausting the appeal remedy available to him, the writ petitioner has approached this Court by way of filing this writ appeal.
Therefore, we find that there is no error in the order passed by the learned single Judge in W.P. (MD).No.1374 of 2017, dated 09.10.2017.

No costs.
